learn.b: A computer takes input (like typing), processes it, and gives output (like text on the screen). It can also store data for later.
Hardware is the parts you can touch, like the screen and keyboard. Software is the programs and apps that tell the hardware what to do.
Computers use only 0s and 1s. One 0 or 1 is a bit. Eight bits make one byte, which can store one letter like A.

qs.q: Which one is an input device?
qs.why: A keyboard sends data into the computer, so it is an input device.

qs.q: Which one is software?
qs.why: A web browser is a program, and programs are software.

qs.q: How many bits are in one byte?
qs.why: One byte is made of 8 bits.

qs.q: Which digits do computers use to store all data?
qs.why: Computers use the binary system, which has only 0 and 1.

qs.q: A monitor is an output device.
qs.why: A monitor shows information coming out of the computer.

qs.q: Match each device to its type
Put these in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: The operating system (OS) is the main software of a computer. It manages the hardware and lets apps run. Windows, macOS, Linux, Android and iOS are operating systems.
A file holds data, like a photo or a document. Folders keep files organized. The file extension, like .jpg or .txt, shows the file type.
Save your work often so you do not lose it. A backup is an extra copy of your files in another place, in case something breaks.

qs.q: Which of these is an operating system?
qs.why: Linux is an operating system; the others are apps.

qs.q: What does a file extension like .jpg tell you?
qs.why: The extension shows the file format, here an image.

qs.q: What is the main job of an operating system?
qs.why: The OS manages the computer's parts and lets programs run.

qs.q: What is a backup?
o: An extra copy of your files
qs.why: A backup is a copy kept safe in case the original is lost.

qs.q: Folders help you organize files.
qs.why: Folders group related files together so they are easy to find.

qs.q: Match each file extension to its type
Put these steps in order to save a new document

learn.b: The CPU (central processing unit) runs instructions and does calculations. A faster CPU can do more work each second.
RAM is short-term memory. It holds what you are using now and is erased when the power is off. Storage (SSD or hard drive) keeps files even when the computer is off.
The motherboard connects all the parts together. The GPU handles graphics. The power supply gives the parts electricity.

qs.q: Which part is called the brain of the computer?
qs.why: The CPU runs instructions and does the calculations.

qs.q: What happens to data in RAM when the computer is turned off?
qs.why: RAM is temporary memory and loses its data without power.

qs.q: Which part connects all the main components together?
qs.why: The motherboard is the main circuit board that links the parts.

qs.q: Which part is mainly responsible for graphics?
qs.why: The GPU (graphics processing unit) draws images and video.

qs.q: An SSD keeps your files when the computer is turned off.
qs.why: An SSD is permanent storage, so data stays without power.

qs.q: Match each part to its job
Put these storage sizes in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: Shortcuts save time. Ctrl+C copies, Ctrl+V pastes, and Ctrl+Z undoes your last action. On a Mac, use Command instead of Ctrl.
Apps are programs for a task, like writing or drawing. Updates fix bugs and add features, so install them when your computer asks.
If a computer is frozen or acting strange, restarting it often helps. Also check cables, close extra programs, and save your work often.

qs.q: Which shortcut copies selected text on Windows?
qs.why: Ctrl+C copies what you selected.

qs.q: Which shortcut undoes your last action?
qs.why: Ctrl+Z reverses the last action.

qs.q: What is a good first step when a computer freezes and acts strange?
qs.why: Restarting clears many temporary problems.

qs.q: Why should you install software updates?
o: They fix bugs and add features
They slow the computer on purpose
qs.why: Updates fix problems and improve the software.

qs.q: Ctrl+V pastes the text you copied.
qs.why: Ctrl+V inserts copied or cut content.

qs.q: Match each shortcut to its action
Put these steps in order to copy a sentence to another document

learn.b: The internet is a huge group of connected computer networks around the world. Computers on it share information with each other.
The internet is the network itself. The World Wide Web is one service that runs on it: websites you open in a browser. Email is another service.
Your device is a client that asks for information. A server is a computer that stores websites and sends them to you when you ask.

qs.q: What is the internet?
qs.why: The internet connects many networks around the world.

qs.q: What is a web browser?
o: A program used to view websites
qs.why: Browsers like Chrome and Firefox open and show websites.

qs.q: Which one is a server's job?
o: Store websites and send them to users
qs.why: Servers hold website data and send it when a client asks.

qs.q: Which of these uses the internet but is not the web?
qs.why: Email is a separate service that runs on the internet.

qs.q: The World Wide Web and the internet are exactly the same thing.
qs.why: The web is just one service that runs on the internet.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order when you open a website

learn.b: Every device on the internet has an IP address, like 192.168.1.1. It works like a home address so data knows where to go.
People remember names like example.com, but computers use numbers. DNS translates a website name into its IP address.
Data is split into small pieces called packets. Each packet travels on its own path and the pieces are put back together at the end.

qs.q: What does DNS do?
o: Turns website names into IP addresses
qs.why: DNS translates names into the numbers computers use.

qs.q: What is an IP address?
o: A number that identifies a device on a network
qs.why: An IP address identifies a device so data can reach it.

qs.q: What are packets?
o: Small pieces of data sent across a network
qs.why: Data is split into packets for travel across the network.

qs.q: Which one looks like an IPv4 address?
qs.why: IPv4 addresses are four numbers separated by dots.

qs.q: DNS is often compared to a phone book for the internet.
qs.why: It looks up a name and gives back the matching number.

qs.q: Match each term to what it does
Put these in order when you visit a website by name

learn.b: HTML builds the structure of a page. CSS makes it look nice with colors and layout. JavaScript makes it interactive.
A URL is a web address, like https://example.com/page. HTTP is the set of rules browsers and servers use to talk. HTTPS is the secure version.
A search engine like Google helps you find pages. Cookies are small files a site saves in your browser to remember things, such as your login.

qs.q: Which language builds the structure of a web page?
qs.why: HTML defines headings, paragraphs, links and other page structure.

qs.q: What is CSS mainly used for?
qs.why: CSS controls colors, fonts and layout.

qs.q: What does the S in HTTPS stand for?
qs.why: HTTPS is HTTP with security, which encrypts the connection.

qs.q: What is a cookie in a browser?
o: A small file a website saves to remember you
qs.why: Cookies store small bits of data, like a login or settings.

qs.q: JavaScript is commonly used to make web pages interactive.
qs.why: JavaScript runs in the browser to react to clicks and more.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these in order from the start of a URL to the end

learn.b: Use long passwords with different words, numbers and symbols. Use a different password for each site. A password manager can remember them for you.
Scam emails and texts often rush you or ask for passwords. Do not click strange links. Check who really sent the message.
Everything you post leaves a trail. Think before sharing personal details like your address, school or phone number, because the internet can keep it for a long time.

qs.q: Which password is the strongest?
qs.why: It is long and mixes words, numbers and symbols.

qs.q: You get an email that says click now or lose your account. What should you do?
o: Be careful and check if it is real
qs.why: Rushing you is a common scam sign, so verify first.

qs.q: What is a digital footprint?
o: A shoe print on a keyboard
The trail of information you leave online
qs.why: Your posts and activity online make up your footprint.

qs.q: Which is the best way to handle many passwords?
o: Write them on a public site
qs.why: A password manager stores unique passwords safely.

qs.q: It is safe to share your home address with anyone online.
qs.why: Personal details can be misused, so share them only with people you trust.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order when you get a strange link

learn.b: Cybersecurity means protecting computers, accounts and data from people who should not have access. It keeps your private information safe.
Security has three goals. Confidentiality: only the right people see data. Integrity: data is not changed by mistake or by attackers. Availability: data and systems work when you need them.
No single tool is perfect, so we use many layers: strong passwords, updates, firewalls, backups and careful habits. If one layer fails, another can still help.

qs.q: What does confidentiality mean in security?
o: Only authorized people can see the data
qs.why: Confidentiality keeps information private from people who should not see it.

qs.q: What does availability mean in security?
o: Data is copied to a phone
Systems and data work when needed
qs.why: Availability means you can use the system and data when you need them.

qs.q: Why do we use many layers of defense?
o: If one fails, others still protect
It is required by law in every home
qs.why: Layers give backup protection when one measure fails.

qs.q: Which of these is a goal of cybersecurity?
qs.why: Cybersecurity exists to protect systems, accounts and data.

qs.q: Integrity means data stays correct and is not changed without permission.
qs.why: Integrity protects data from unwanted changes.

qs.q: Match each security goal to its meaning
Put these in order from weakest to strongest protection

learn.b: A strong password is long, such as a phrase of several random words, and is not a name or birthday. Never reuse the same password on different sites.
Two-factor authentication (2FA) asks for something more than a password, like a code from your phone. Even if someone learns your password, they still need the second step.
A password manager is an app that creates and stores a different strong password for each account. You only need to remember one main password.

qs.q: Which password is the best choice?
qs.why: It is long, random and hard to guess.

qs.q: What is two-factor authentication?
o: Using two passwords that are the same
A second step to prove it is you
qs.why: 2FA adds a second proof, like a code, besides the password.

qs.q: Why should you not reuse one password everywhere?
o: If one site leaks it, all accounts are at risk
qs.why: A leaked reused password lets others try it on your other accounts.

qs.q: What does a password manager do?
o: Stores strong unique passwords for you
qs.why: It saves and fills in unique passwords so you do not have to remember them.

qs.q: It is safe to tell your password to a friend.
qs.why: Passwords should be kept private to protect your account.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order to set up a safer account

learn.b: Phishing is a trick message that pretends to be a bank, a game or a friend to make you share a password or click a bad link. Signs are urgency, spelling mistakes and odd sender addresses.
Malware is harmful software. A virus attaches to files and spreads. Ransomware locks your files and demands money. Spyware secretly watches what you do.
Do not click unknown links or open surprise attachments. Download apps only from trusted stores. Use antivirus software and keep it updated.

qs.q: What is phishing?
o: A fast way to download games
A trick message that tries to steal information
qs.why: Phishing tries to fool you into giving up private data or clicking bad links.

qs.q: Which is a common warning sign of a phishing email?
o: It comes from a known friend and has no link
It uses your correct full name only
It creates urgency, like act now or lose access
qs.why: Pressure to act quickly is a classic sign of a scam.

qs.q: What does ransomware do?
o: Locks your files and demands payment
qs.why: Ransomware locks files and asks for money to unlock them.

qs.q: Where should you download apps from?
qs.why: Official stores check apps, which lowers the risk of malware.

qs.q: Spyware secretly collects information about what you do.
qs.why: Spyware is made to watch activity without your knowledge.

qs.q: Match each threat to its description
Put these steps in order when you get a suspicious message

learn.b: Encryption scrambles data so only someone with the right key can read it. HTTPS uses encryption, so people on the same Wi-Fi cannot read what you send to a secure site.
A firewall is like a guard at the door of a network. It checks incoming and outgoing traffic and blocks what breaks its rules.
Updates fix security holes, so install them quickly. Backups keep a copy of your files, so you can recover them after a problem. A common rule is to keep copies in more than one place.

qs.q: What does encryption do to data?
o: Makes it unreadable without the key
qs.why: Encryption scrambles data so only key holders can read it.

qs.q: What is the main job of a firewall?
qs.why: A firewall allows or blocks traffic based on security rules.

qs.q: Why are software updates important for security?
qs.why: Updates patch weaknesses that attackers could use.

qs.q: Which sign in the browser shows a site uses an encrypted connection?
qs.why: HTTPS and the padlock show the connection is encrypted.

qs.q: A backup helps you recover files if your device is lost or locked by malware.
qs.why: A separate copy lets you restore your data.

qs.q: Match each tool to its purpose
Put these steps in order for a safe update routine

learn.b: AI is when computers do tasks that usually need human thinking, like understanding speech, recognizing pictures or making decisions.
You use AI when a phone unlocks with your face, when a map finds the fastest route, or when a video app suggests what to watch.
Today's AI is narrow: it is good at one kind of task. A chess AI plays chess very well but cannot cook or drive. It does not think like a person.

qs.q: What is AI?
o: Computers doing tasks that usually need human thinking
qs.why: AI covers computers doing tasks like understanding language or images.

qs.q: Which is an everyday example of AI?
qs.why: Face unlock uses AI to recognize your face.

qs.q: What does narrow AI mean?
o: AI that is good at one specific kind of task
AI that can do every task
qs.why: Narrow AI is built for specific tasks only.

qs.q: A video app suggests videos you may like. This is mostly an example of:
qs.why: Recommendation systems use AI to predict what you may enjoy.

qs.q: Today's AI systems think and feel exactly like humans.
qs.why: Current AI finds patterns in data but does not think or feel like people.

qs.q: Match each AI use to its example
Put these in order from simplest to most complex

learn.b: In machine learning, a computer is not given every rule. It learns patterns from many examples. For instance, it sees thousands of cat photos and learns what a cat looks like.
Training is when the model learns from data. Testing checks it on new examples it has not seen. Good results on new data show it really learned.
Supervised learning uses examples with correct labels. Unsupervised learning finds groups in data without labels. Reinforcement learning learns by trying actions and getting rewards.

qs.q: What does machine learning mainly use to learn?
qs.why: Models learn patterns from lots of data.

qs.q: Why do we test a model on new data?
o: To check it learned well, not just memorized
qs.why: New data shows whether the model works beyond its training examples.

qs.q: Which type of learning uses data with correct labels?
qs.why: Supervised learning learns from labeled examples.

qs.q: A game agent learns by trying moves and getting points. This is:
qs.why: Reinforcement learning uses rewards for good actions.

qs.q: More good quality data can often help a model learn better.
qs.why: Good, varied examples help the model find true patterns.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these machine learning steps in order

learn.b: A neural network is a model loosely inspired by the brain. It has layers of small connected units. Data goes in, passes through the layers, and an answer comes out. Deep learning uses many layers.
A large language model, or LLM, is trained on huge amounts of text. It learns to predict the next word, which lets it write answers, summarize and translate.
Chatbots can make mistakes and sometimes state wrong things with confidence. This is called a hallucination. Always check important facts with a reliable source.

qs.q: What is a neural network inspired by?
qs.why: Neural networks are loosely inspired by how brain cells connect.

qs.q: What does deep learning mean?
o: Using many layers in a neural network
qs.why: Deep learning uses neural networks with many layers.

qs.q: What does an LLM mainly learn to do?
o: Predict the next word in text
qs.why: Large language models learn patterns in text to predict what comes next.

qs.q: What is a hallucination in AI?
o: A confident answer that is actually wrong
qs.why: AI can produce made-up or incorrect information that sounds sure.

qs.q: You should always check important facts from a chatbot with a reliable source.
qs.why: Chatbots can be wrong, so verification is important.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these in order when you ask a chatbot a question

learn.b: AI learns from data made by people. If the data is unfair or missing some groups, the AI can be unfair too. This is called bias, and builders must work to reduce it.
Do not share private details like passwords or your address with an AI tool. Also be honest: if you use AI for school work, follow your teacher's rules and say so.
A good prompt is clear and gives details: what you want, who it is for, and the format. You can ask follow-up questions to improve the answer.

qs.q: Why can AI be biased?
o: It learns from data that may be unfair or incomplete
qs.why: Biased or missing data can lead to unfair results.

qs.q: What should you avoid sharing with an AI tool?
qs.why: Private details could be stored or misused, so keep them to yourself.

qs.q: Which prompt is clearer?
o: Write 3 simple tips for a school talk on recycling
qs.why: It says the task, the topic, the audience and the amount.

qs.q: If AI is used on school work, what is the best action?
o: Follow your teacher's rules and be honest
qs.why: Honesty and following the rules are part of responsible AI use.

qs.q: AI answers are always correct and never need checking.
qs.why: AI can make mistakes, so important answers should be checked.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order to use AI for research well

learn.b: A network is two or more devices connected so they can share data. A home network might connect phones, laptops and a printer.
A LAN (local area network) covers a small place like a home or school. A WAN (wide area network) covers a big area. The internet is the biggest WAN.
A router connects your network to the internet and sends data in the right direction. A switch connects devices inside a LAN. A modem links your home to your internet provider.

qs.q: What is a network?
qs.why: A network links devices so they can exchange data.

qs.q: Which network usually covers a home or school?
qs.why: A LAN covers a small local area.

qs.q: Which device connects your home network to the internet and directs data?
qs.why: A router sends data between your network and the internet.

qs.q: What is the biggest WAN in the world?
qs.why: The internet connects networks across the entire world.

qs.q: A switch connects multiple devices inside a local network.
qs.why: Switches link wired devices within a LAN.

qs.q: Match each device to its job
Put these in order from smallest to largest network

learn.b: Ethernet uses cables to connect devices. Wired links are usually fast, stable and secure. Common cables are Cat5e and Cat6.
Wi-Fi sends data through radio waves, so devices can connect without cables. It is convenient, but walls and distance can make the signal weaker.
Bandwidth is how much data can move per second, measured in Mbps. Latency, or ping, is the delay before data starts arriving. Low latency matters for gaming.

qs.q: Which type of connection is usually the most stable?
qs.why: Wired Ethernet has fewer interruptions than wireless.

qs.q: What does Wi-Fi use to send data?
qs.why: Wi-Fi uses radio waves in the air.

qs.q: What does bandwidth measure?
o: How much data can move per second
qs.why: Bandwidth is the data capacity of a connection, such as Mbps.

qs.q: What is latency?
qs.why: Latency is the time delay, often called ping.

qs.q: Walls and long distance can weaken a Wi-Fi signal.
qs.why: Obstacles and distance reduce radio signal strength.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these speed units in order from smallest to largest

learn.b: A protocol is a set of rules that devices follow to talk to each other. TCP/IP is the main family of rules for the internet.

TCP sends data carefully and checks that it arrives, which is good for web pages. UDP is faster but does not check, which is good for live video and games. HTTP is used for web pages and SMTP for sending email.
An IP address can change and shows where a device is on a network. A MAC address is a unique ID built into the network hardware. DHCP automatically gives devices an IP address.

qs.q: What is a protocol?
o: A set of rules for communication
qs.why: Protocols define how devices send and understand data.

qs.q: Which protocol checks that data arrives correctly?
qs.why: TCP confirms delivery and resends missing data.

qs.q: What does DHCP do?
qs.why: DHCP hands out IP addresses on a network.

qs.q: A MAC address is:
o: A unique ID built into network hardware
qs.why: Each network adapter has a unique hardware address.

qs.q: UDP is often used for live video and games because it is fast.
qs.why: UDP skips delivery checks, which lowers delay.

qs.q: Match each protocol to its use
Put these in order when your device joins a Wi-Fi network

learn.b: Most homes have a modem from the provider and a router that creates the Wi-Fi. Often both are in one box. Place the router in a central, open spot for the best signal.
Change the default router password, use WPA2 or WPA3 security, and choose a strong Wi-Fi password. Keep the router firmware updated. Use a separate guest network for visitors.
If the internet stops working, first check the cables and lights. Then restart the router and modem. Test another device to see if the problem is one device or the whole network.

qs.q: Where is a good place for a Wi-Fi router?
qs.why: A central open place spreads the signal better.

qs.q: Which Wi-Fi security setting is recommended?
qs.why: WPA2 and WPA3 are modern, stronger security methods.

qs.q: What is a good first step when the internet stops working?
o: Check cables and restart the router
qs.why: Simple checks and a restart solve many problems.

qs.q: Why use a guest network?
o: It keeps visitors apart from your main devices
qs.why: A guest network protects your own devices and files.

qs.q: You should keep the default router password unchanged.
qs.why: Default passwords are widely known, so change them.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order to fix a no-internet problem

learn.b: A desktop PC has a motherboard, CPU, RAM, storage, power supply and often a graphics card. All of them sit in the case.
The motherboard is the main board that all parts plug into. The power supply unit (PSU) changes the electricity from the wall into the power each part needs.
CPUs and GPUs get hot when they work. Fans, heatsinks or liquid coolers move heat away. If a PC gets too hot, it slows down to protect itself.

qs.q: Which part do all other components plug into?
qs.why: The motherboard connects every component.

qs.q: What does the PSU do?
qs.why: The power supply unit converts wall power for the computer's parts.

qs.q: Why does a PC need cooling?
o: To remove heat from hot parts
qs.why: Heat can slow or damage parts, so it must be moved away.

qs.q: Which part holds all the components inside a desktop PC?
qs.why: The case houses the motherboard and other parts.

qs.q: A heatsink helps take heat away from a CPU.
qs.why: Heatsinks spread heat so fans can blow it away.

qs.q: Match each part to its job
Put these in order of how power reaches the CPU

learn.b: CPU speed is measured in GHz. A core is a part of the CPU that can do work. More cores help with doing many tasks at once. Intel and AMD are two main CPU makers.
RAM is fast, temporary memory for running programs. More RAM lets you keep more apps and browser tabs open. Typical sizes are 8 GB, 16 GB or 32 GB.
Cache is a tiny, very fast memory inside the CPU. It keeps data the CPU is using often so it does not need to wait for RAM.

qs.q: What is CPU clock speed measured in?
qs.why: GHz tells how many billions of cycles a CPU does per second.

qs.q: What can having more CPU cores help with?
o: Handling many tasks at the same time
qs.why: Multiple cores can work on different tasks together.

qs.q: What is RAM used for?
qs.why: RAM is the working memory for active programs.

qs.q: Where is cache memory located?
qs.why: Cache is very fast memory built into the CPU.

qs.q: RAM keeps your files after the computer is turned off.
qs.why: RAM is temporary, so its content is lost when power is off.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these in order from fastest to slowest memory

learn.b: A hard disk drive (HDD) stores data on spinning disks. It is cheap and big but slower. A solid-state drive (SSD) has no moving parts, so it is faster, quieter and uses less power.
Storage is measured in gigabytes (GB) and terabytes (TB). 1 TB equals about 1,000 GB. A game or video can take many GB, so choose enough space.
A GPU makes images for the screen and is very good at doing many small jobs at once. Gamers and video editors want a strong GPU. Many CPUs also include basic built-in graphics.

qs.q: Which drive type has no moving parts?
qs.why: SSDs store data on chips, with no spinning disks.

qs.q: Which is usually faster?
qs.why: SSDs read and write much faster than HDDs.

qs.q: About how many GB are in 1 TB?
qs.why: 1 terabyte is about 1,000 gigabytes.

qs.q: What is a GPU mainly used for?
qs.why: The graphics processing unit renders images, video and games.

qs.q: An HDD uses spinning disks to store data.
qs.why: A hard disk drive has spinning platters inside.

qs.q: Match each part to its feature
Put these in order from smallest to largest storage size

units.title: Building and Caring for a PC

learn.b: Building a PC means fitting the CPU, RAM and storage onto the motherboard, putting it in the case, adding the power supply and connecting the cables. Check that parts are compatible, such as the CPU socket fitting the motherboard.
Turn off and unplug the PC before opening it. Static electricity can harm parts, so touch a metal part of the case first or use an anti-static wristband. Do not force parts into place.
Dust slows airflow and makes PCs hot. Clean the fans gently with compressed air. Keep vents clear, and keep drivers and system updates current.

qs.q: What should you check before buying a CPU and motherboard together?
qs.why: The CPU must fit the motherboard's socket type.

qs.q: What should you do before opening a PC case?
qs.why: Removing power protects you and the parts.

qs.q: Why is dust a problem inside a PC?
o: It blocks airflow and causes heat
qs.why: Dust blocks fans and vents, so parts overheat.

qs.q: What is a safe way to clean dust from fans?
o: Use a wet cloth on live parts
qs.why: Compressed air removes dust without touching delicate parts.

qs.q: You should force a part into its slot if it does not fit at first.
qs.why: Forcing parts can break them; check the direction and compatibility instead.

qs.q: Match each term to its meaning
Put these steps in order to build a basic PC
items: Mount the board in the case

learn.h: The cloud is other people's computers
learn.b: The cloud means using computers and storage in big data centers over the internet, instead of only on your own device. Companies like Amazon, Microsoft and Google run them.
When you store photos online, stream a movie, or edit a document in a browser with friends, you use the cloud. Your files can be reached from any device with a login.
The cloud can be cheap to start, easy to share and quick to grow. You pay only for what you use. Remember you need internet access to reach it.

qs.q: What is the cloud?
o: Computers and storage you use over the internet
qs.why: The cloud is remote computing and storage reached through the internet.

qs.q: Where does cloud data live?
qs.why: Cloud services run on servers inside data centers.

qs.q: Which is an everyday example of cloud use?
o: Storing photos online and opening them on any device
qs.why: Online photo storage keeps files on remote servers.

qs.q: What do you usually need to reach cloud files?
qs.why: Cloud services are reached over the internet.

qs.q: In cloud computing, you often pay only for what you use.
qs.why: Many cloud services are billed by usage.

qs.q: Match each cloud service to its example
Put these in order when you save a file to cloud storage

learn.b: Software as a Service gives you a ready-to-use app in a browser, like Gmail or Google Docs. The company runs everything; you just use it.

Platform as a Service gives developers a place to build and run apps without managing servers. Infrastructure as a Service gives you basic building blocks, like virtual servers and storage, and you manage more of it.
A public cloud is shared and owned by a provider. A private cloud is used by one organization only. A hybrid cloud mixes both.

qs.q: Which is an example of SaaS?
qs.why: SaaS delivers finished apps like web email.

qs.q: What does IaaS provide?
o: Basic computing resources like virtual servers
qs.why: Infrastructure as a Service rents servers, storage and networking.

qs.q: What does PaaS mainly help developers do?
o: Build and run apps without managing servers
qs.why: PaaS provides a platform so developers focus on code.

qs.q: What is a hybrid cloud?
o: A mix of public and private cloud
qs.why: Hybrid cloud combines public and private cloud resources.

qs.q: A private cloud is used by a single organization.
qs.why: Private clouds are dedicated to one group.

Put these in order from most managed by you to least managed by you

learn.b: Virtualization lets one physical server run many virtual machines (VMs). Each VM acts like its own computer. This lets providers share hardware and save money.
Scalability means adding or removing resources as needed. If a website suddenly gets many visitors, the cloud can add servers quickly, then remove them when traffic drops.
Providers have data centers in many regions. Copying data to more than one place, called redundancy, helps keep services running if one place has a problem.

qs.q: What does virtualization allow?
o: Running many virtual machines on one physical server
qs.why: One physical server can host many separate virtual computers.

qs.q: What does scalability mean in the cloud?
o: Adding or removing resources as needed
qs.why: Cloud resources can grow or shrink with demand.

qs.q: Why do providers keep copies of data in more than one place?
o: Redundancy keeps services working after a failure
qs.why: Redundancy protects against loss or outages.

qs.q: A site gets a sudden rush of visitors. What helps in the cloud?
qs.why: Cloud scaling can add capacity quickly.

qs.q: A virtual machine acts like a separate computer.
qs.why: A VM has its own OS and apps, even though it shares hardware.

learn.b: The provider protects the data centers and hardware. You are responsible for your own account, passwords and settings. Use strong passwords and two-factor login.
Check who can see your files. Share links only with the people who need them, and use view-only access when possible. Do not store secrets in public places.
Many services have a free amount and charge after that. Watch your storage and usage so there are no surprise bills. Keep a backup of important files, as the cloud is not a magic guarantee.

qs.q: Who is responsible for your cloud account password?
qs.why: Users must protect their own login details.

qs.q: Which setting adds safety to a cloud account?
qs.why: Two-factor login adds a second proof beyond the password.

qs.q: When sharing a cloud file, what is a good practice?
o: Share only with needed people, view-only when possible
Post the link in a public chat
qs.why: Limit access to what is necessary.

qs.q: How can you avoid surprise cloud bills?
qs.why: Tracking usage helps you stay within free or planned limits.

qs.q: Keeping a backup of important files is still a good idea when using the cloud.
qs.why: Services can fail or accounts can be lost, so extra copies help.
